body.x: The world's largest IT and technology exhibition, CES 2025, concluded on January 10 in Las Vegas, USA. The Seoul Pavilion, organized on a record scale, achieved remarkable results and showcased the collaborative efforts of Seoul’s startup ecosystem.

Spanning 1,040 square meters in Eureka Park, CES’s startup-focused exhibition space, the Seoul Pavilion featured 16 institutions, including three districts (Gangnam, Gwanak, and Geumcheon), five startup support organizations, and eight universities.
Interview with Kim Yangsung | Produced by AVING News

Among the Seoul Pavilion participants, the G-Valley Industrial Association (GVIA), a startup incubator and business support organization based in Geumcheon-gu, showcased nine companies, including three Innovation Award winners. Established in 2007, G-Valley is home to over 14,000 companies with a strong focus on IT, manufacturing, and startups, aiming to become Korea's "future Silicon Valley."

To support these companies, Geumcheon-gu collaborates with the Seoul Business Agency (SBA) to facilitate participation in international exhibitions, such as CES, providing financial assistance, pre-show consultations, and post-show performance tracking.

body.cap: Kim Yangsung, Head of Corporate Support Team at Geumcheon-gu Office, interviews with AVING News at CES 2025 in Las Vegas | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q: This is G-Valley’s first time participating in CES. How does it feel to represent the district here?

Kim Yangsung: While we have participated in regional exhibitions like those in Singapore, CES offers a much larger stage. We decided to join this global platform to reflect the aspirations of our local companies to reach broader markets. The scale and innovation on display here have been truly eye-opening, showcasing the rapid pace of technological advancements.
G-Valley companies can compete on the global stage, and CES offers an excellent opportunity for competition and collaboration.

body.cap: Kim Yangsung, Head of Corporate Support Team at Geumcheon-gu Office, interviews with AVING News at CES 2025 in Las Vegas | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q: What criteria were used to select the participating companies from G-Valley?

Kim Yangsung: G-Valley is home to over 14,000 companies. This year, we received applications from numerous firms and evaluated them based on their innovation and technological capabilities. After a rigorous selection, we chose nine companies showcasing the strongest potential to impact the global market.
Q: Can you highlight some notable companies from G-Valley participating in CES 2025?

Kim Yangsung: Among the standout companies is AFS Inc., which introduced the ‘AFS 3D,’ an AI solution for diagnosing hair loss. This system automates hair and scalp analysis, providing precise data for effective treatments. It has garnered significant interest from global medical professionals.

Another notable company is OTITON MEDICAL Co., Ltd., which earned an Innovation Award for its smart thermometer equipped with a sensor for diagnosing ear infections. The company’s integration of AI enables it to assess the severity of infections and provide tailored recommendations, attracting the attention of healthcare professionals.

body.cap: Kim Yangsung, Head of Corporate Support Team at Geumcheon-gu Office, interviews with AVING News at CES 2025 in Las Vegas | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q: What plans does Geumcheon-gu have to maximize the impact of CES 2025?

Kim Yangsung: We are committed to ensuring this opportunity extends beyond the exhibition. We will analyze data on potential buyers and provide companies with actionable insights to facilitate successful follow-ups.

Additionally, we aim to digitize internal workflows for participating companies and offer IT and smart work training programs. This will enable them to operate more efficiently. We are also exploring initiatives like AI voucher programs to help businesses adopt customized AI solutions at reduced costs.
CES 2025 has proven to be a valuable starting point for positioning G-Valley as a global innovation hub, and we will continue to support our companies in their journey toward international success.
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
